title: Patient perspectives on the use of artificial intelligence in radiological diagnostics: An adapted survey to assess current status and acceptance
summary: Methods that can be summarised under the term "artificial intelligence" (AI) are playing an increasing role in image-based diagnostics (radiology). It is hoped that AI will increase the accuracy of diagnoses, improve the efficiency of work processes and optimise patient care overall. A questionnaire-based study will be used to record patients' opinions, experiences and attitudes towards the use of AI in radiology. This will help to identify the key factors that influence trust and acceptance of AI-based applications in clinical practice.
conditions: Patients for whom a radiological examination (X-ray, sonography, CT, MRI) is planned.

interventions.name: Patients with a planned radiological examination who are asked to complete a questionnaire on the use of AI in radiology for study purposes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Planned performance of a radiological imaging examination (e.g. X-ray, ultrasound, CT, MRI).
- Declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Insufficient knowledge of German.
- Severe cognitive impairment
- Acute serious illness where it is not possible to complete the questionnaire before the examination.
